plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit high-beta software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and semis (MUU).
Trim income holding (QQQI) to reduce concentration.
This builds a significant cash buffer for safety.
Focus shifts to capital preservation and low volatility.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and concentrating on safer assets, but this also limits upside potential and may result in lower growth.

plan: Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta software/semis.
Trim income holding (QQQI) to manage concentration.
Initiate a new position in AMD, a quality tech name.
This balances risk reduction with targeted growth opportunities.
A modest cash buffer is maintained for flexibility.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% monthly. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a quality name, aiming for steadier returns with controlled drawdowns. Upside is moderate.

plan: Trim income holding (QQQI) to free up capital.
Increase positions in leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta software/semis.
Add a new position in AMD for concentrated tech exposure.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for maximum growth potential.
A smaller cash buffer means higher exposure and risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets significant growth, aiming for around 4% monthly, by increasing leverage and concentration in high-conviction tech names. It accepts substantially higher potential drawdowns and the risks associated with leveraged ETFs, requiring strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names.
Increase allocation to income-focused ETF (QQQI).
This shifts the portfolio towards generating steady monthly distributions.
The focus is on capital preservation and reliable income over growth.
A larger cash buffer is maintained for stability.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly through distributions, prioritizing stability and yield. It minimizes volatility by exiting leveraged and high-beta positions, aiming for consistent income rather than capital appreciation. NAV can still decline in market downturns.
